newsitem.title: USA: Govt must remove our nuke waste - Consumers Power.
newsitem.headline: Govt must remove our nuke waste - Consumers Power.

text.p: The U.S. government must take away spent nuclear fuel from power plants and not just pay utilities to store the radioactive waste at their sites, said Michael Morris, president of Consumers Power Co, a subsidiary of CMS Energy Corp.
"You've got my money. You take the waste," Morris said in a brief interview, after speaking at a nuclear power conference hosted by Energy Daily.
He was referring to the $12 billion the government has already collected from nuclear utilities in a trust fund that was meant to pay for a nuclear waste dump to be ready in 1998.
The Energy Department is now deciding how to live up to its obligation under a 1982 law to take over responsibility for disposing of spent fuel from power plants in 1998.
One way out would be to pay utilities to store their own spent fuel until the department has built a dump, which is not expected to be ready before 2010.
"We don't want our money back," Morris said.
He predicted that Congress might be able to pass legislation next year that would force the government to build an interim storage site.
Similar legislation passed the Senate this year, but the margin was too narrow to override a veto promised by President Clinton.
"We're not veto proof yet," said Morris. But he said "it's possible" that once out of the election year, Clinton might back down from his opposition to putting the waste in Nevada.
